This paper describes software (FR10A and AFRA) that has been developed for this purpose in The National Grid Company plc.

articleTitle: Intelligent phase comparison carrier protection
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: Conventional phase comparison carrier protection mainly consists of three units-starting unit, phase discriminator and trip relay. The phase discriminator is the brain of phase comparison protection. It compares the measured phase shift of the high-frequency carrier current signals /spl theta/ at the two ends of the protected transmission line with the stability angle /spl phi/, to determine whether or not to trip the line. It is known that /spl theta/ varies under different power system operating conditions and fault conditions. Since in conventional phase comparison protection /spl phi/ is set off-line and cannot change on-line to adapt to various operating and fault conditions, the possibility of maloperation exists. In order to overcome the shortcoming we have developed an artificial neural network (ANN) approach for phase comparison carrier protection. There are some advantages which are inherent in ANN such as excellent noise immunity, robustness, fault-tolerance and generalization capability. A multilayer feedforward network (MFFN) approach for phase comparison protection is presented in this paper. Such an approach has excellent generalization capability. Digital simulation has been carried out using the Electromagnetic Transient Program to verify the performance of the proposed approach. Results show that the approach has the ability to adapt to various operating and fault conditions.

articleTitle: A generic communications language-four years of experience
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: The introduction of the microprocessor to protective relays and other technological advances have made it feasible to add communication facilities to relays, enabling remote monitoring by direct extraction of available data and remote control of the items of plant connected to the relays. Power utilities have shown a marked change in attitude by an ever increasing interest in using relay communication features. Principally to remove the need for external monitoring and control devices, such as transducers and auxiliary relays, thus reducing functional duplication, wiring, commissioning and hence lowering cost. As yet there is no accepted international standard for communication links with protective relays. Work within the IEC has resulted in the proposal, IEC870-5 companion standard 103, as the informative interface for protection and control relays. This proposed standard embodies the generic principles developed and used within our generic protocol. This paper describes a generic communication system developed specifically for remote monitoring and control of protective relays within the substation environment, changes in attitude towards communications, practical experience and it's influence on IEC870-5-103.

articleTitle: Training and development of protection engineering staff
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: This paper reviews the changing needs of staff involved in discharging work associated with protection technology, and examines the consequences of decisions made by various groups of personnel in this area. The changing nature of the protection product itself is now impacting on the skills required, and the ever present pressure to minimise costs is affecting the number, and the nature, of staff available. Training which leads to an authorisation to discharge duties is relevant in many areas and ensures competency; in this case training is likely to be vocationally linked and outcome based. Manufacturers should be involved in training exercises where new equipment is introduced, although as equipment becomes more widespread, more use of in-house is appropriate. Simulators provide an excellent route to enabling access training and authorisation. Simulation of plant and the substation environment gives, effectively, hands-on experience of typical equipment and test procedures. Open learning, on-going learning (Continuing Professional Development) and learned society activities all provide viable training routes to utilities staff which are compatible with the work environment. A graphical approach to the evaluation of training needs, its progress and effect has been described. This method allows training to be reviewed in the light of new developments. The role of information technology and artificial intelligence are likely to greatly influence training methods and requirements in the future.

articleTitle: International timekeeping for power system users
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: People in our modern society are using navigational systems for position and velocity determination, geodesy, surveying and route determination for aircraft, marine vessels and land vehicles. Accurate and precise timekeeping is finding increasing application by power system engineers and researchers. Precise timekeeping is used in power systems for time synchronizing disturbance recorders, synchronizing measurements across an entire interconnection and locating transmission line faults. With microsecond synchronization, power system phase angles can be measured in real-time. Power system phase angles form the state vector of the power grid. Knowledge of the state vector can increase the performance of state estimators. This paper discusses the present state of international timekeeping from a power systems viewpoint. Recent political and technical achievements are discussed which promise NAVSTAR-Global Positioning System and Global Orbiting Navigation Satellite System availability well into the 21st Century.

articleTitle: A new 11 kV protection maintenance procedure using an expert system software tool
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: An expert system software tool, ProMEX, to support field operators in the maintenance of 11 kV feeder protection schemes has been introduced into service by Yorkshire Electricity. The tool assesses the test results obtained on-site and suggests the appropriate courses of action combined with 'intelligent' access to documentation to guide users in carrying out the tests. A major benefit provided by the introduction of such a tool is enabling protection maintenance (being a relatively complex area of engineering) to be carried out to consistent and high standards by staff with less expertise in protection, along with an audit trail for the maintenance programme. The role and the functionality of the ProMEX protection maintenance tool are described. The benefits that Yorkshire Electricity has gained from introduction of the tool are discussed along with the procedures put in place to enable the tool to be introduced in a way that enable these benefits to be realised.

articleTitle: An expert system to evaluate the operating response of the distance relays during a fault
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: This paper describes an expert system designed to analyse the response to a short circuit fault, of all the distance protection schemes located within a region of a power network. The expert system identifies which, if any, relays have maloperated, and assesses the response of the distance relays that did not trip correctly. The paper details the different expert system models that were built to locate the faulted feeder and also to evaluate the validity of the relays that responded to the fault. The evaluation includes finding whether any communication channels have failed, and if they have, determine whether the relay failed to send/receive the intertrip/block signals.

articleTitle: Test procedures for protection devices
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: Power system protection device testing requires a wide spectrum of test procedures. The classical division into routine testing and type testing is preserved. In addition to the tests required by national and international regulations, the entire range of communication and protection functions of protection devices needs to be tested as part of the software type testing procedure. The application of modern computer technology in connection with transients programs is the basis for the performance of complex test procedures. Analysis systems support the test engineer and thereby reduce the effort in terms of staff skill and time. At the same time, the testing depth and quality is enhanced and the system response of the protection device is made transparent to the manufacturer and to the user. Cost-effective yet high-quality testing of protection devices is now practically impossible without the application of system modelling programs.

articleTitle: An advanced simulation and testing environment for design, application and performance assessment of protection equipment
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the requirements for the performance assessment of power system protection equipment, taking into account advances in simulation technology and related tools. The basic features of the computer simulation and testing environments needed to meet the requirements are also discussed. Examples of different hardware and software developments of new simulation environments undertaken by the author and his research team are outlined. Some most relevant experiences are pointed out in conclusion.

articleTitle: The uses of protection performance data within a transmission system
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: Data on power system protection equipment defects can be used to provide support for asset life predictions and the establishment of refurbishment, replacement, reconditioning and monitoring strategies. The requirement to compile protection fault performance and protection defect statistics therefore, has been established through the necessity to make protection policy and investment decisions on a rational basis. This paper describes the UK's National Grid Company (NGC) system for collecting and analysing protection fault performance and defect data and provides illustrations of how the information is being used.

articleTitle: Network protection and control using standardised communications
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: This paper describes the communication standard for power network control and protection. It also points out that the development in communication technologies will secure in the future to cope with the evolution to new protection and control architectures. An example of the hierarchical power system protection and control strategies using communications is also included in this paper.

articleTitle: Concepts and realisation of fault recording system in a large power station
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: The perception in the Water and Electricity Department, Abu Dhabi, UAE, has grown stronger on judicious monitoring by a dedicated system of the operation of switching, regulating and protection equipment. Due to the degree of success in fault analysis depending heavily on the accuracy of data captured by the recording system used, the application of standalone fault recorders is now entering a new era on utility power systems. As a result of their design and manufacture being perceived with innovative hardware architectures and software breakthroughs, fault recorders have become more powerful in application and taken a winning place as the mainstay of information recording at every power station and grid substation built by the department. The focal point of this paper is the summary account of technical perspectives put into design and engineering aspects of the new fault recording facilities.

articleTitle: Protection implications from a communications system upgrade
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: This paper addresses issues faced and strategies adopted for the implementation of an optical fibre communications link and the interfacing of a replacement for an existing 330 kV line protection in the Snowy Mountains scheme, South Eastern Australia. The paper discusses: the communications upgrade and protection options; formulation of a combined protection/control philosophy; combined protection/communications functional specification; application of the protection; and commissioning tests.

articleTitle: Network Interface Modules for microprocessor relays integration into a substation automation system
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: Network Interface Modules (NIM) allow the integration of microprocessor based relays and other intelligent electronic devices using different communication protocols into a substation integration system. Modular design of the NIM and software and hardware configurability of the communications allows the use of a universal module for interface with addressable or nonaddressable relays through RS-232, RS-485, copper or fiber optic cables. The basic components of a typical system of a substation integration system architecture and their essential functions are described. These are: the network master; the backup network master, and the Network Interface Module. NIM hardware and programming are also discussed.

articleTitle: A technico-economically oriented maintenance strategy for digital protections
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: As a consequence of the rapid rise of digital protection relays within the Netherlands, Dutch utilities are having increasing doubts about their existing maintenance strategies for protection relays. The utilities have the impression that modern digital relays offer possibilities for improving the efficiency of protection relay maintenance and that the maintenance costs can be reduced by switching over to a new maintenance strategy. In order to underpin this impression KEMA Transmission and Distribution has started a research program. The program has led to the drawing up of a new maintenance strategy for digital relays. In this paper the new maintenance strategy is presented.

articleTitle: Power system simulator for the training of protection engineers
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: A wide range of power system simulators and relay test sets are now available for the testing of protection relays. The vast majority of these are designed for testing an individual relay, very few are designed for testing a complete protection and control scheme. The simulator described in this paper is suitable for the comprehensive testing of both integrated and coordinated protection and control schemes and individual relays and control equipment. The simulator can also be used for training engineers and students on the application and operation of protection and control equipment. A prototype version of this simulator was installed in 1994 at the National Grid (NGC) Training Centre in Eakring, Nottinghamshire.

articleTitle: GPS synchronised end-to-end tests of transmission line teleprotection schemes in the ESKOM network
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: GPS synchronised end-to-end testing of power transmission line teleprotection schemes provide a suitable means to verify the complete functionality of a power system protection scheme, consisting of a relay at either end of the transmission line and a communications channel linking the two relays. Successful field trials were conducted in the ESKOM network.

articleTitle: Benefits of distribution automation and performance results from a network trial
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: Typical medium voltage distribution systems have developed slowly over many years and essentially comprise of circuit breakers at primary substations feeding a series of isolatable step down transformers. Customers have been demanding better continuity of supply and performance from the network and utilities have been investigating ways of responding without the need for large capital investment. Improvements in switching devices, protection relays and telecontrol in recent years have made the implementation of distribution automation schemes cost effective and the benefits are being realised through a number of installations. This paper explores the benefits of distribution automation, details the equipment required and raises a number of issues relating to a real installation.

articleTitle: An operational simulator for testing EHV and MV protective relays
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: The development of protection systems for EHV and MV transmission makes it necessary to update equipment testing devices. New digital relays operate faster and cover an increasingly broad frequency spectrum. Their acceptance and routine tests, the analysis of operating incidents and even the study of new principles require a tool which can accurately generate transient currents and voltages over a large bandwidth. Therefore Electricite de France (EDF) has developed an open loop digital transient network analyser tool (DTNA). The DTNA allows tests of the EHV transmission protective relay. In view of the complexity of the transient modelling in the DTNA, it can appear that the integration of this code in the environment of a protection-unit test laboratory presents major difficulties. Nothing of the kind, since the development of the DTNA from its original design integrates the automated management of the test databases, the man-machine graphical interface, the plotting and the post-processing of the simulation results, which now allows an operator used to former analogue test benches to use the DTNA without any difficulty. The introduction of new models (voltage generator with a nonlinear frequency, a nonlinear amplitude, and a superposition of harmonics; hysteresis and remanent models for transformers) allows MV transmission protective relay tests.

articleTitle: New simulation models to dynamically test impedance relays
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: Modern protective relays are becoming more sophisticated and faster as time progresses. Relay test systems also become more sophisticated and flexible. Yet some protective relay manufacturers claim that there is no need to test numerical relays, such as impedance relays, as the operating characteristics are accurate and do not change with time. Why then test numerical relays in the same way as it has always been done? This paper takes a critical look at the conventional test techniques and the associated simulation models. More realistic test models are discussed and a test system that combines all the necessary test models is introduced.

articleTitle: A model based technique for the comprehensive validation of power system protection operation
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: Following a disturbance on the power network, protection engineers are required to determine if the protection schemes operated correctly. To aid protection engineers in this task, they have access to supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system data and fault recorder data. This paper reports on a decision support system (DSS) for protection engineers which will automatically analyse this data to provide a comprehensive report on the protection scheme operation. The DSS comprises of two knowledge based systems which interpret the SCADA system data and a model based diagnosis module that can utilise both SCADA system data and fault recorder data. This paper concentrates in particular on the model based aspect, which provides the comprehensive analysis of the protection scheme operations. A case study is presented demonstrating the depth of diagnosis possible.

articleTitle: Development of a transient stability protection system for Eskom's Matimba power station
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: This paper describes the special protection system that was developed for Eskom's Matimba power station (South Africa). The power transfer of the Matimba interconnected power system is limited to 90% of the station's full load output capacity due to the fact that faults on the power system will lead to network pole slipping and network breakdown at higher loads. The conventional solution of increasing the tie line strength or installing more lines was every expensive and an alternative solution had to be found. By implementing "generator dropping" or tripping a generator on severe faults, network pole slipping can be prevented. The protection scheme detects when faults on the power system will lead to a network pole slipping and disconnects a generator/s as well as trip line reactors, ensuring stable operation.

articleTitle: Overcurrent protection co-ordination: a modern approach for modern devices
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (Conf. Publ. No. 434)
abstract: One of the most demanding tasks in applying power system protection is to choose suitable settings for primary or backup overcurrent relays. These must offer adequate sensitivity, acceptable fault clearance times and discrimination of protective relays at various locations and under variable system operating conditions. The relay co-ordination task is to make relays remote from the location of a fault operate more slowly than those which are required to trip. The difference in relay operating times is the co-ordination or grading margin. This paper briefly reviews established approaches to relay co-ordination and it offers a revised approach to address problems faced by many power system protection engineers today, especially when dealing with different relay designs. The approach is well suited to the use of spreadsheet methods, which enables it to be used very easily.
